title: Run game day: hosted overload + load shedding simulation (scenarios + results + follow-ups)
creator: Rafael Mendes
project: Reliability Program: Hosted circuit breakers + load shedding
description:
Objective
Validate that hosted overload protection (breaker + load shedding + graceful degradation) behaves predictably under realistic failure modes, and that oncall can detect/mitigate without causing retry storms or cascading failures.

This game day is explicitly NOT a perf benchmark; it is an operability + failure semantics + coordination exercise.

Date / logistics
- Planned window: 2025-12-03 10:00–12:00 PT
- Environment: prod-like staging (hosted-api-stg) with perf-canary traffic generator + controlled fault injection
- Scope limited to us-east + eu-west staging regions

Roles
- Incident Commander (IC): Sean Gallagher (Eng SRE)
- Ops lead / breaker operator: Christine Wong (Eng SRE)
- Routing owner: Peter Holtz (Routing reliability)
- Runtime owner: Sofia Ivanova (Runtime scheduling)
- Observability lead: Aisha Bello
- Comms / notes: Connor O'Brien
- Observers: Amara Diallo, Benji Okafor, Elena Popov

Pre-req checklist (must be green before start)
- Dashboards available and linked from runbook:
  - shed rate (%), breaker open rate, admission reject rate
  - runtime queue depth (prefill/decode), token/sec saturation, KV cache pressure proxy
  - 429/503 error breakdown by route/model/tier
- incident-bot breaker state announcements enabled in #incidents-stg
- Retry-After header enabled for overload responses in staging
- Fallback routing configured for 2 test tenants (one allowed, one disallowed) to validate policy guardrails
- Support-facing error taxonomy drafted (sanity check only; no external comms)

Success criteria (what we want to prove)
1) Tail lat under burst stays bounded via early rejection (no runaway timeouts).
2) Error semantics are stable:
   - 429 used for tenant/plan/rate admission rejections where applicable
   - 503 used for capacity/overload conditions
   - overload error codes present + correlation IDs present
   - Retry-After present for shed responses
3) No feedback loop / retry storm: system shed/reject does not amplify downstream saturation.
4) Tier/tenant isolation holds: one noisy tenant cannot degrade other tenants beyond configured shared limits.
5) Operators can answer within 10 minutes:
   - Is it real overload vs dependency brownout?
   - Which layer is applying backpressure (gateway vs routing vs runtime)?
   - What safe levers exist (caps, feature flags, regional canary rollback)?

Scenario scripts
Scenario A: Burst traffic (no dependency failures)
- Purpose: validate admission controls + breaker thresholds; verify dashboards/alerts + error taxonomy.
- Setup:
  - Traffic generator ramps concurrency over 8 minutes while varying prompt lengths (p50 300 tokens, p95 4k tokens) and streaming on.
  - Target endpoints: /v1/chat.completions + /v1/completions (70/30 split)
- Fault injection: none (pure burst)
- Expected behavior:
  - queue depth rises, shed kicks in before p99 latency runaway
  - breaker opens for impacted route/model when saturation persists
  - responses include stable overload codes + Retry-After

Scenario B: Downstream dependency brownout (auth/usage enforcement latency)
- Purpose: validate circuit breaker semantics when dependency latency spikes (prevent request pile-up at gateway and protect runtime).
- Setup:
  - steady moderate load (baseline) + introduce 10% traffic spike
  - inject 800–1500ms p95 latency into usage enforcement path for one tenant (simulated)
- Expected behavior:
  - dependency health signal triggers targeted shedding for the affected route/tenant
  - healthy tenants unaffected
  - operators can distinguish dependency brownout from GPU saturation using dashboards

Scenario C: Regional capacity dip + fallback routing
- Purpose: validate smart routing fallback behavior when breaker is open; ensure loop prevention + bounded attempts.
- Setup:
  - reduce available runtime capacity in us-east staging (simulate node drain) while keeping eu-west healthy
  - enable fallback policy for Tenant A: model X in us-east -> model X in eu-west (allowed)
  - Tenant B: no fallback allowed (should get overload errors)
- Expected behavior:
  - Tenant A sees elevated latency but lower error rate (bounded retries; no loops)
  - Tenant B sees 503 overload with Retry-After (no silent timeouts)
  - routing logs indicate single fallback attempt max, then return overload

During-exercise operator actions (scripted prompts)
- Verify breaker state transitions are posted by incident-bot
- Confirm alerts fire only after agreed burn thresholds (avoid paging noise)
- Use runbook actions in order (no “random toggling”):
  1) confirm overload source via saturation vs dependency panels
  2) apply safe caps (streaming concurrency cap, max_tokens cap) via policy flags
  3) if needed, roll back canary toggle for breaker evaluation in one region
- Record each action with timestamp and observed effect within 5 minutes

Artifacts to capture
- Timeline with timestamps (trigger -> detection -> decision -> mitigation -> recover)
- Dashboard screenshots (or permalinks) at key points
- Example raw responses showing overload error payload + correlation ID + Retry-After
- List of confusing signals / missing links in runbooks
- Follow-up tickets with owners + severity
acceptance_criteria:
- Game day completed in staging with at least 3 scenarios (burst, dependency brownout, regional capacity dip).
- Notes include: scenario configs, expected vs observed behavior, decision timeline, and concrete follow-up actions.
- At least 5 sample overload responses captured with correlation_id + error code + Retry-After.
- Follow-up bugs/tasks created for any gaps (runbook, dashboards, routing loop prevention, SDK guidance) with owners assigned.
results_summary:
Executed 2025-12-03 in hosted-api-stg.

Scenario A (Burst): PASS with minor gaps
- Observed:
  - p99 latency stayed bounded once shedding engaged; timeouts decreased vs baseline run without early shedding.
  - breaker opened on /v1/chat.completions for model redwood-llama-70b (stg) after sustained queue depth.
  - 503 overload responses included correlation_id and stable overload code.
- Issues:
  - ~7% of 503 overload responses missing Retry-After header on the streaming route (likely gateway path mismatch).
  - Dashboard for “shed rate by model” was high-cardinality and slow to load; operators had to use aggregate view.

Scenario B (Dependency brownout): PARTIAL PASS
- Observed:
  - dependency latency spike correctly surfaced on dependency health panel.
  - gateway admission rejected affected tenant earlier, reducing end-to-end request pile-up.
- Issues:
  - error code mapping sometimes returned generic 503 without dependency-specific overload code (harder to diagnose).
  - alerting: one page fired for global 503 rate even though impact was primarily one tenant (need tenant-aware gating or annotation).

Scenario C (Regional capacity dip + fallback): PASS with tuning notes
- Observed:
  - Tenant A successfully failed over to eu-west in ~65% of requests during peak drain; remainder got 503 with Retry-After.
  - Tenant B correctly did not fallback and received overload responses.
  - routing loop prevention worked (no repeated bounce between regions).
- Issues:
  - fallback added ~400–700ms median latency; acceptable but we should update docs/runbook to set expectation.
  - correlation between breaker-open events and routing fallback events not obvious in dashboards (need cross-panel links or shared correlation dimension).

Operator outcomes
- IC and Ops lead were able to identify overload source within ~6 minutes for Scenario A and ~9 minutes for Scenario B.
- Runbook was usable but missing direct links to 2 dashboards and the policy toggle names were not consistent across docs.
